actual_noncompliance_witness287.procedure_delivered_verbatim: Use § 522(d)(1) for a residence or burial plot, (d)(2) for one motor vehicle, (d)(3) for the listed personal-use goods, (d)(4) for personal-use jewelry, (d)(6) for trade tools or professional books, and (d)(9) for a professionally prescribed health aid. Also retain (d)(5) for every asset. For the whole named asset, claim the lesser of its value and $27,900 under (d)(1), $4,450 under (d)(2), $700 under (d)(3), $1,875 under (d)(4) for one debtor or $3,750 for jointly owned jewelry of two debtors, or $2,800 under (d)(6); (d)(9) protects the full value. Under (d)(5), use $15,425 for one debtor and, for jointly owned property of two debtors, sum the two separately available ceilings to a maximum whole-asset claim of $30,850. Do not return a debtor's half-interest as the asset-level amount.
actual_noncompliance_witness287.avoid_when_delivered_verbatim: Do not output §§ 522(b), 522(d), or 522(m) as exemption alternatives. A firearm is not a (d)(3) household-good category, and a medical item is not a (d)(9) health aid without professional prescription. Do not automatically double the specific (d)(1)-(d)(3) or (d)(6) ceiling merely because two debtors jointly own the asset.
